# Statistical models for spatial data

## Exercise 10.1 {-}

following the `lm` example of Section 10.2 use a random forest model
to predict `SID` values (e.g. using package **randomForest**), and 
plot the random forest predictions against observations, along
with the $x=y$ line.

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
system.file("gpkg/nc.gpkg", package="sf") |>
    read_sf() -> nc
nc |> mutate(SID = SID74/BIR74, NWB = NWBIR74/BIR74) -> nc1
library(randomForest) |> suppressPackageStartupMessages()
r = randomForest(SID ~ NWB, nc1)
nc1$rf = predict(r)
plot(rf~SID, nc1)
abline(0, 1)
```

## Python

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor

nc = gpd.read_file("data/nc/nc.shp")
nc1 = nc.assign(SID=nc.SID74 / nc.BIR74, NWB=nc.NWBIR74 / nc.BIR74)

r = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=500, oob_score=True, random_state=7392)
r.fit(nc1[["NWB"]], nc1.SID)
nc1["rf"] = r.oob_prediction_  # out-of-bag predictions, as predict(r) gives in R

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.scatter(nc1.SID, nc1.rf)
ax.axline((0, 0), slope=1, color="black")
ax.set_xlabel("SID")
ax.set_ylabel("rf")
plt.show()
```
:::

## Exercise 10.2 {-}

Create a new dataset by randomly sampling 1000 points from the
`nc` dataset, and rerun the linear regression model of section
10.2 on this dataset. What has changed?

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
pts = st_sample(nc, 1000)
nc2 = st_intersection(nc1, pts)
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc1) |> summary()
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc2) |> summary()
```

## Python

```{python}
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# 1000 random points in the state; each gets the attributes of the county it is in
pts = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    geometry=gpd.GeoSeries(nc1.geometry.union_all())
        .sample_points(1000, rng=7392).explode(ignore_index=True),
    crs=nc1.crs)
nc2 = gpd.sjoin(pts, nc1, how="inner", predicate="intersects")

m1 = smf.ols("SID ~ NWB", nc1).fit()
m2 = smf.ols("SID ~ NWB", nc2).fit()
print(m1.summary().tables[1])
print(m2.summary().tables[1])
```
:::

we see that the standard error has decreased with a factor 3 (sqrt(10)).

For prediction interval widths:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc1) |>
  predict(nc1, interval = "prediction") -> pr1
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc2) |>
  predict(nc1, interval = "prediction") -> pr2
mean(pr1[,"upr"] - pr1[,"lwr"])
mean(pr2[,"upr"] - pr2[,"lwr"])
```

## Python

```{python}
def mean_width(m, kind):
    d = m.get_prediction(nc1).summary_frame(alpha=0.05)
    return (d[f"{kind}_ci_upper"] - d[f"{kind}_ci_lower"]).mean()

print(mean_width(m1, "obs"))  # prediction interval, nc1 model
print(mean_width(m2, "obs"))  # prediction interval, nc2 model
```
:::

no change, as this dominated by the residual variance;

Confidence intervals for the predicted means:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc1) |>
  predict(nc1, interval = "confidence") -> pr1
lm(SID ~ NWB, nc2) |>
  predict(nc1, interval = "confidence") -> pr2
mean(pr1[,"upr"] - pr1[,"lwr"])
mean(pr2[,"upr"] - pr2[,"lwr"])
```

## Python

```{python}
print(mean_width(m1, "mean"))  # confidence interval of the mean, nc1 model
print(mean_width(m2, "mean"))  # confidence interval of the mean, nc2 model
```
:::

drops for larger dataset, as this is dominated by the standard
errors of estimated coefficients.

## Exercise 10.3 {-}

Redo the water-land classification of section 7.4 using `class::knn`
instead of `lda`.

Preparing the dataset:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
tif <- system.file("tif/L7_ETMs.tif", package = "stars")
library(stars)
(r <- read_stars(tif))
set.seed(115517)
pts <- st_bbox(r) |> st_as_sfc() |> st_sample(20)
(e <- st_extract(r, pts))
plot(r[,,,1], reset = FALSE)
col <- rep("yellow", 20)
col[c(8, 14, 15, 18, 19)] = "red"
st_as_sf(e) |> st_coordinates() |> text(labels = 1:20, col = col)
rs <- split(r)
trn <- st_extract(rs, pts)
trn$cls <- rep("land", 20)
trn$cls[c(8, 14, 15, 18, 19)] <- "water"
```

## Python

```{python}
import rioxarray
import xarray as xr
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap

x = rioxarray.open_rasterio("data/L7_ETMs.tif").astype("float64")

# the 20 sample points used in the R solution (set.seed(115517), st_sample)
tp = pd.read_csv("data/l7_train_pts.csv")
bands = [f"X{i}" for i in range(1, 7)]
vals = x.sel(x=xr.DataArray(tp.x), y=xr.DataArray(tp.y), method="nearest").values.T
trn = pd.DataFrame(vals, columns=bands)

water = [8, 14, 15, 18, 19]  # identified visually, 1-based
cls = np.where(np.isin(np.arange(1, 21), water), "water", "land")

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
x.sel(band=1).plot(ax=ax, cmap="gray", add_colorbar=False)
for i, (xx, yy, c) in enumerate(zip(tp.x, tp.y, cls), start=1):
    ax.text(xx, yy, str(i), color="red" if c == "water" else "yellow")
plt.show()
```
:::

estimation and prediction happen in one command:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
library(class)
as.data.frame(trn) |> select(X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> tr 
as.data.frame(rs) |> select(X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> test
rs$cls = knn(tr, test, trn$cl, k = 5)
plot(rs["cls"])
```

## Python

```{python}
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier

X, Y = np.meshgrid(x.x.values, x.y.values)
test = pd.DataFrame(x.values.reshape(6, -1).T, columns=bands)

def show(pred, title):
    plt.imshow((pred == "water").reshape(X.shape), cmap="Blues",
               extent=(x.x.min(), x.x.max(), x.y.min(), x.y.max()))
    plt.title(title)
    plt.show()

# estimation and prediction in two steps (fit, predict)
knn = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5).fit(trn, cls)
pred = knn.predict(test)
print(pd.Series(pred).value_counts())
show(pred, "cls")
```
:::

## Exercise 10.4 {-}

For the `nc` data: estimation

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
st_centroid(nc1) |> st_coordinates() -> cc
bind_cols(nc1, cc) |> transmute(X=X, Y=Y, SID=SID, NWB=NWB) -> nc2
(lm0 <- lm(SID ~ NWB, nc1)) |> summary()
(lm1 <- lm(SID ~ NWB+X+Y, nc2)) |> summary()
(lm2 <- lm(SID ~ NWB+X+Y+I(X^2)+I(Y^2)+X*Y, nc2)) |> summary()
```

## Python

```{python}
import spherely

# centroids on the sphere (sf uses S2 for lon/lat data by default)
c = spherely.centroid(spherely.from_wkt([g.wkt for g in nc1.geometry]))
nc_xy = nc1.assign(X=spherely.get_x(c), Y=spherely.get_y(c))

lm0 = smf.ols("SID ~ NWB", nc1).fit()
lm1 = smf.ols("SID ~ NWB + X + Y", nc_xy).fit()
lm2 = smf.ols("SID ~ NWB + X + Y + I(X**2) + I(Y**2) + X*Y", nc_xy).fit()
for m in (lm0, lm1, lm2):
    print(m.summary().tables[1])
```
:::

The first order model seems to have significant coordinate effects,
for the second order model none of the coordinate effects are
significant.

Prediction:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
nc1$pr0 <- lm0 |> predict(nc2)
nc1$pr1 <- lm1 |> predict(nc2)
nc1$pr2 <- lm2 |> predict(nc2)
nc1[c("pr0", "pr1", "pr2")] |> st_as_stars() |> merge() |> plot(breaks = "equal")
```

## Python

```{python}
nc1["pr0"] = lm0.predict(nc_xy)
nc1["pr1"] = lm1.predict(nc_xy)
nc1["pr2"] = lm2.predict(nc_xy)

lim = dict(vmin=nc1[["pr0", "pr1", "pr2"]].min().min(),
           vmax=nc1[["pr0", "pr1", "pr2"]].max().max())  # same colour scale
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(12, 3))
for ax, v in zip(axes, ["pr0", "pr1", "pr2"]):
    nc1.plot(ax=ax, column=v, legend=(v == "pr2"), **lim)
    ax.set_title(v)
    ax.set_axis_off()
plt.show()
```
:::

Largely the same pattern is shown in the predictions, some extremes get more
extreme.

For the `knn` on the remote sensing data:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R

```{r}
cbind(as.data.frame(trn), st_coordinates(trn)) |> 
  select(X, Y, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> tr1
as.data.frame(rs) |> transmute(X=x, Y=y, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> test1
rs$cls1 = knn(tr1, test1, trn$cl, k = 5)
cbind(as.data.frame(trn), st_coordinates(trn)) |> 
  transmute(X, Y, X2=X^2, Y2=Y^2, XY=X*Y, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> tr2
as.data.frame(rs) |> 
  transmute(X=x, Y=y, X2=X^2, Y2=Y^2, XY=X*Y, X1, X2, X3, X4, X5, X6) -> test2
rs$cls2 = knn(tr2, test2, trn$cl, k = 5)
rs[c("cls", "cls1", "cls2")] |> merge() |> plot()
```

## Python

```{python}
tr1 = trn.assign(X=tp.x, Y=tp.y)
test1 = test.assign(X=X.ravel(), Y=Y.ravel())
cols1 = ["X", "Y"] + bands
pred1 = KNeighborsClassifier(5).fit(tr1[cols1], cls).predict(test1[cols1])
show(pred1, "cls1")

# note: in the R code, the column X2 = X^2 gets the same name as band X2,
# so band 2 is silently dropped from this second model; we do the same here
def squares(d):
    return d.assign(X2=d.X**2, Y2=d.Y**2, XY=d.X * d.Y)

cols2 = ["X", "Y", "X2", "Y2", "XY", "X1", "X3", "X4", "X5", "X6"]
pred2 = KNeighborsClassifier(5).fit(squares(tr1)[cols2], cls).predict(squares(test1)[cols2])
show(pred2, "cls2")
```
:::

Both models involving coordinates show much worse results!
